title: Chefbook: SDK onboarding recipes (sketch)
content:
Overview
This is a very rough, intentionally pragmatic sketch of a chefbook-style onboarding playbook for new devs integrating with Redwood SDKs. Goal: give devs a tiny set of reproducible "recipes" they can follow from zero -> prototype in 30–90 minutes, plus an ops cheat-sheet for common failure modes. Tone: kitchen shorthand (short steps), actionable commands, and quick fallbacks.

Mise en place (pre-flight)
- account: create org token + API key (link to onboarding emails).
- env: have Node 18+ and Python 3.10 installed.
- tools: curl, jq, docker (optional).
- telemetry: enable local DEBUG=redwood_sdk for first-run logs.

Recipes
1) Hello-generation (5 minutes)
- purpose: verify fundamental network + auth + model selection.
- steps: set REDWOOD_API_KEY, run: curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' -d '{"model":"rwd-compact-1","prompt":"Say hi"}' | jq .
- expected: JSON stream or 200 with text field. If 401 -> check token scope. If timeout -> try region fallback header X-Region: us-east-1.

2) Chat quickloop (15–30 minutes)
- purpose: samples for conversation state, streaming, and function-calling stub.
- skeleton code: short Node and Python snippet in README template (link placeholder).
- tests: simulate 50 short requests locally to exercise batching; check KV-cache header in responses.

3) Embeddings + files (20 minutes)
- purpose: local vector store baseline for docs search.
- steps: run sample script to index 100 markdown files, query similarity.
- metrics to eyeball: tokens/embedding, latency p95, embedding failure %

Rollout & gating recipe (canary)
- preconditions: unit prompt tests + quality evals (small prompt set).
- traffic split: 5% canary for 24h, compare top-level metrics (latency, cost, hallucination score).
- rollback: revert route in console; alert on >5% percentile degradation.

Troubleshooting checklist (kitchen hacks)
- 401 auth -> regenerate token, check org membership.
- 429 rate-limited -> add retries with exponential backoff and jitter; set quota in console.
- high latency occasional -> enable smaller batch size, switch to low-latency model variant.
- unexpected output quality drop -> pin model version, run prompt regression harness.

Developer templates (to drop into repos)
- README snippet: one-paragraph summary + quick curl example + where to get keys.
- .env.example: minimal env vars (REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_REGION, RW_ENV).
- smoke CI job: ephemeral key, run hello-generation and embeddings quick test.

Observability & signals to watch (first week)
- p95 generation latency, tokens-per-second, 5xx rate, streaming disconnects, cost-per-1000-tokens.
- developer-facing: first-call-to-success ratio, time-to-first-token, sample rate of debug logs.

Open questions / TODOs
- bake in language-specific idioms for Go and Rust (currently Node/Py heavy).
- minimal docker image with prebuilt examples for offline hackathons.
- prefilled prompt-sets: create 10 canonical prompts per telemetry surface (search, compose, summarization).

Notes-to-self
- keep recipes short; each recipe should be runnable with copy-paste commands.
- stash a "kitchen-sink" example repo for instructors to demo in 20 minutes.
- align metrics names with console dashboards (ask obs team for canonical names).

References
- linked artifacts above (Jira / PR / Confluence).
- internal Slack thread: #devex-sdk-onboarding (search for "chefbook").

End of sketch — wants review from Liam/Priya for Node/Py code snippets and Marcus for rollout gating language.
